title: Tenant cost fences and instance-class preference for smart routing
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: Multiple customers want stronger per-tenant spend controls that let them optimize for cost (prefer spot / lower-class GPUs) while retaining predictable latency for critical routes. Current routing only supports coarse budget guards and region-tier fallbacks; it doesn't express tenant preferences for GPU class or graceful overage behavior.

Goal: Implement a tenant-scoped "cost fence" and instance-class preference layer in the routing decision pipeline. This will let a tenant specify soft/hard spend caps, a tolerance window (grace buffer), and an ordered preference with weights for instance classes (e.g., a2-highgpu > a1-highgpu > p4d). The router should: 1) honor hard caps (reject + 402-style error), 2) apply soft caps by throttling or routing to cheaper variants with configurable aggressiveness, and 3) use a probabilistic spot acceptance curve to reduce spike evictions.

Core design decisions:
- Policy model: tenant routing policy is a small JSON document stored in the control plane with fields: soft_cap_usd, hard_cap_usd, grace_window_minutes, class_preferences (ordered list with weights), spot_acceptance_threshold (0..1). Policies default to global account-level settings when missing.
- Enforcement surface: Enforcement happens at the routing service before capacity allocation. For soft-cap hits we do preference-based re-routing; for hard-cap hits we short-circuit and return a structured error with guidance and the tenant spend dashboard link.
- GPU class weighting: Implement affinity score = base_score * class_weight * (1 - spend_penalty). This lets the router prefer certain SKUs and gradually degrade to cheaper SKUs as the tenant approaches soft cap. We avoid hard, deterministic fallthrough to prevent latency cliffs.
- Spot hedging: Use a simple probabilistic accept-reject for spot-backed slots driven by spot_acceptance_threshold and recent eviction rate. This aims to balance cost vs risk; it is controllable per-tenant.
- Telemetry: Emit spend_rollup_{tenant}, spend_rate_{tenant}, fallback_rate_{tenant}, spot_eviction_rate_{tenant}, per_route_latency_slo_breaches. Add Grafana dashboards and per-tenant burn-rate alerts.
- Console UX: Expose tenant policy editor in Console -> Cost controls with 3 presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) and an "edit JSON" advanced view. Include live estimate of projected monthly savings vs SLO risk.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Control plane schema changes: routing_policies table; migration script to populate defaults.
2) Router changes: policy fetch cache with TTL, scoring function for instance classes, soft/hard cap checks, probabilistic spot acceptance. Provide well-structured error codes for SDKs.
3) Billing integration: hook spend_rollup to billing pipeline to ensure near-realtime spend used for enforcement (eventual consistency tolerances documented).
4) Console + API: UI for editing policies, API endpoints: GET/PUT /v1/tenants/{id}/routing_policy.
5) Testing: unit tests for scoring, integration tests with simulated spend, e2e against staging fleet with mixed spot/on-demand SKUs. Chaos test: inject spot evictions and verify fallback rate.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strictly enforcing hard caps in near-realtime requires tight coupling with billing; we accept a small eventuality window (30 seconds) to avoid large engineering scope.
- Deterministic fallback to cheapest SKU reduces variance but can cause latency cliffs; we prefer weighted/probabilistic fallbacks to smooth latency.
- Per-tenant policy complexity must be limited to keep config simple for customers; the initial schema is intentionally small and opinionated.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged across runtime-2.4. Stage 1: internal tenants + canary customers (opt-in). Stage 2: gradual enable by tenant tier with monitoring of fallback_rate and SLA breaches. Stage 3: GA with console presets and documentation.

Links & artifacts: design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-example-routing-policy-design; implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8219; test harness: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/pipelines/routing-policy-canary; Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference/d/tenant-routing/tenant-spend-and-fallback
acceptance_criteria: Control plane stores per-tenant policy and serves GET/PUT API with schema validation
Router applies soft/hard cap logic using near-realtime spend and returns structured errors when hard cap hit
Weighted instance-class scoring implemented and exercised in unit tests
Probabilistic spot acceptance reduces eviction-related SLO breaches in staging (observed fallback_rate decrease)
Console shows policy editor with presets and links to spend dashboard
End-to-end test demonstrating a tenant route is routed to cheaper SKU when soft cap hit without exceeding hard cap
